RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel composition doesn't point anywhere useful here. You are a woman and the appointee is a woman, so sex can't explain why she was preferred over you. An all-female panel is also unremarkable in laboratory medicine and nursing-adjacent fields, where women are the majority. Raising it would read as grasping and would undermine your credibility on the point that actually has substance.

That point is this: you appear more qualified on paper (PhD versus master's, eight years running a section), the stated rationale rests on vague wording like "broad leadership experience," and your request for written reasons has gone unanswered for two weeks. Chase that in writing, ask what criteria were scored and how, and keep it factual.
